tests.title: Copied HTML table displays as columns in the reading pop-up
tests.userStory: A user copies a table from a browser and invokes Read clipboard text aloud.
tests.setupInstrumentation: Put a three-column HTML table with two data rows on the macOS clipboard in both text/plain and text/html flavors; launch the local Electron app and invoke the tray action.
steps: Inspect the visible overlay table and its accessible rows/cells
Confirm displayed words match the speech text
expectedResults: Header and data cells occupy three aligned columns
The pop-up remains usable at its normal width
Spoken/alignment text contains each cell once in reading order
tests.evidence: Local Electron Chromium loaded the real overlay page and preload. Three aligned columns, row grouping, canonical reading order, and wide-table scrolling passed in table-qa-results.json. Screenshot: qa-screenshots/table-three-columns.png. The production app's native tray action was not clicked because it was actively reading the user's document.
tests.remaining: Run the packaged build's Read clipboard text aloud action with a copied table after the current reading finishes.

tests.title: Selected-text capture preserves the same table layout
tests.userStory: A user selects browser content containing a table and starts reading via the selected-text action.
tests.setupInstrumentation: Open a local browser fixture with prose before and after a table; select all relevant content; use Read selected text or the shortcut with Accessibility permission.
steps: Inspect the overlay from first paragraph through the table and following paragraph
expectedResults: Table headers and values remain in rows and columns
Prose and inline formatting remain legible
No cell text is lost or duplicated
tests.evidence: The selected-text JXA code passes HTML to the same speakText/overlay renderer, whose table layout passed in local Electron Chromium. The production app was observed actively reading the screenshot's content, so a new native capture would interrupt it.
tests.remaining: Select a table in a frontmost source app and invoke Read selected text in the packaged build after playback ends.

tests.title: Plain text and hostile HTML remain safe
tests.userStory: A user can still read plain clipboard text, and copied markup cannot execute in the pop-up.
tests.setupInstrumentation: Test a plain-text-only clipboard item, then a controlled HTML table containing script/style/event-handler/link/image markup; inspect the sandboxed overlay.
steps: Read plain text and verify it appears
Inspect DOM and check for script execution, navigation, and external requests
expectedResults: Only allowed table and text nodes render
No script, image, link target, or arbitrary attribute survives
tests.evidence: Local Electron Chromium screenshots qa-screenshots/plain-text-regression.png and qa-screenshots/table-sanitized.png. DOM inspection found zero active/attribute nodes, no script execution, and zero external HTTP(S) requests; plain text rendered unchanged.
tests.limitation: Clipboard input was controlled in memory so the user's real pasteboard was not modified.
